answer_text:
Assuming the curve is the standard one arch of the cycloid, i.e. \(0\le t\le 2\pi\):

\[
x=a(t-\sin t),\qquad y=a(1-\cos t)
\]

Differentiate:

\[
dx=a(1-\cos t)\,dt,\qquad dy=a\sin t\,dt
\]

Then

\[
x\,dy-y\,dx
= a(t-\sin t)\cdot a\sin t\,dt-a(1-\cos t)\cdot a(1-\cos t)\,dt
\]

\[
= a^2\left[(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2\right]dt
\]

Simplify the bracket:

\[
(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2
= t\sin t+2\cos t-2
\]

So

\[
\int x\,dy-y\,dx
= a^2\int_0^{2\pi} \left(t\sin t+2\cos t-2\right)\,dt
\]

Now integrate:

\[
\int \left(t\sin t+2\cos t-2\right)dt
= -t\cos t+3\sin t-2t
\]

Thus

\[
\int_0^{2\pi} x\,dy-y\,dx
= a^2\left[-t\cos t+3\sin t-2t\right]_0^{2\pi}
\]

Evaluate:

\[
= a^2\left[-2\pi(1)+0-4\pi\right]
= -6\pi a^2
\]

Therefore, with the natural orientation given by increasing \(t\),

\[
\boxed{-6\pi a^2}
\]

If the opposite orientation is intended, the value is \(\boxed{6\pi a^2}\).
